reason: The goal is to give the potato stems room, and the cargo mesh may provide a support for them.
expectation: I expect the mesh to form some kind of support around the potato trough, though I’m not sure how it will be arranged.

alternatives.reason: Harvesting the lettuce fits the chapter’s introduction, but the potato goal is more immediate.

effect: The mesh supports the spreading potato stems, and the next goal is to taste the first harvest.
reaction: The support is a satisfying use of the mesh; I’m curious about the lettuce harvest.
reason: The scissors and lettuce trough are the only gameplay combination offered, and they fit the new harvest goal.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce for the first harvest, though preparing it to eat may take another step.

effect: The scissors produced fresh lettuce leaves, which can now be taken to the galley for the tasting goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to have the first harvest, though the result is brief.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley is the only gameplay action offered and fits the goal of tasting them.
expectation: I expect to prepare or taste the lettuce at the galley, though I don't know exactly what will happen.

effect: The lettuce became part of the first fresh meal, completing the harvest goal and the chapter.
reaction: The green smell against the barren view is a vivid, satisfying payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the first fresh meal was most worthwhile: the sensory detail made the long wait for food feel tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cutting the lettuce was a brief, predictable step with little detail of its own.

surprise.text: The cargo mesh became a support for the spreading potato stems while the tubers remained covered below.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; the mesh, scissors and galley each had a clear practical purpose.

continue.text: I would continue, partly to see how the potato crop develops and what else the expedition discovers. This chapter's final image made me curious about life there.
